OC-Free-Model-Video

Use OpenRouter's free router in OpenCode for small coding tasks and experiments.

1. Install OpenCode

On macOS with Homebrew, run:

brew install anomalyco/tap/opencode

If you already have OpenCode, skip this step. Other platforms can use the installation guide.

2. Connect your OpenRouter key

Create an API key at OpenRouter. Then launch OpenCode:

opencode

Inside its terminal interface, type /connect, choose OpenRouter, and paste the key. OpenCode saves provider credentials separately from your config.

3. Set the free router as your default

Search and select openrouter/openrouter/free in the model picker.

4. Test it

Exit OpenCode and run:

opencode models openrouter
opencode run -m openrouter/openrouter/free "Reply with: setup works"

The model list should include openrouter/openrouter/free. A reply confirms that authentication and routing work.

5. Use it in a project

From your project directory, start:

opencode -m openrouter/openrouter/free

Try a small task: "Read the README and explain how to run this project." Use /models to switch models later.

6. Model capability reference

The free router dynamically selects models based on your request. Here are the capabilities you can expect from models commonly rotated in:

Model Tool Calling Vision Context Typical Use
Mistral 7B Yes No 8K Simple tasks
Gemma 2 9B Yes No 8K Coding help
Qwen 2.5 7B Yes No 32K Long context
Phi-3 Mini Yes Yes 4K Multimodal

Because the model can change between requests, always test critical capabilities like tool calling in your specific session. Use /models to pin to a specific model when you need consistency.

9. Rate limit handling

  • Free router requests are subject to OpenRouter rate limits. Expect 429 errors under load.
  • Read the Retry-After header (seconds) and pass it to a delay before retrying.
  • Implement exponential backoff in scripts: 1s, 2s, 4s, 8s, max 30s.
  • Cache responses when the same prompt recurs to avoid redundant calls.
  • If a task is urgent or long-running, temporarily switch with /models to a paid model you're comfortable with.

10. Starter projects

Small projects well-suited for free-router experimentation:

README Explainer

Read a project's README and generate a 2-paragraph summary plus setup checklist.

opencode -m openrouter/openrouter/free
"Read the README and summarize how to run this project"

Code Refactor

Give the free router a single function and ask it to improve readability without changing behavior.

opencode -m openrouter/openrouter/free
"Refactor this to be more readable — keep the same output: refactor_me.py"

CSS Animation Generator

Ask for a small CSS snippet and a demo HTML file for a specific animation effect.

opencode -m openrouter/openrouter/free
"Create a pure-CSS shimmer sweep effect on a text label and a demo HTML file"

Data Formatter

Convert a CSV to JSON, normalize field names, or extract columns from a data file.

opencode -m openrouter/openrouter/free
"Normalize column names to camelCase and output JSON: data/sample.csv"

CLI Wrapper

Build a tiny CLI tool that wraps a public API (e.g., a weather or exchange-rate endpoint).

opencode -m openrouter/openrouter/free
"Build a CLI that calls the Open-Meteo API and prints the forecast for a city arg"

11. If it fails

  • A model-not-found error: confirm the full ID openrouter/openrouter/free above and restart OpenCode.
  • An authentication error: reconnect your OpenRouter key with /connect.
  • Rate limit (429): wait before retrying and follow the retry delay in the error headers.
  • Output too long: add a length or complexity constraint to the prompt.
